label: alleged
text: Union Minister Jitendra Singh alleged that the Cockroach Janta Party's founder and co-convenor received foreign funding from US donors and Pakistani politicians, which the party dismissed as baseless claims from officials lacking accountability. PTI and other outlets report.

sources.articleText:
Union Minister Jitendra Singh alleges that the Cockroach Janta Party received funding from US-based donors and Pakistani politicians, prompting Congress to demand evidence from the Centre
Union Minister Jitendra Singh alleges that CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and strategist Ashutosh Ranka received money from US-based donors and Pakistani politicians.
Delhi Police summoned CJP spokespersons Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka over alleged violations linked to protests against the SIR exercise.
Congress leader Priyank Kharge questioned the Centre's allegations and challenged it to provide evidence of foreign funding.

sources.title: Govt accuses CJP of taking US, Pakistan funds; outfit fires back - India Today
sources.articleText:
Union Minister Jitendra Singh has accused Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke of receiving funds from US-based donors and the party's co-founder Ashutosh Ranka of getting financial support from Pakistani politicians and other handlers to fuel anti-government campaigns in India.
The allegations triggered a sharp response from the CJP, which hit back at the Union Minister, questioning the credibility of statements made by those holding high constitutional and political offices.
Singh claimed that foreign-funded non-governmental organisations (NGOs), deep-state operatives and organisations working against India's interests were coordinating efforts to influence public discourse and manufacture narratives against the government.

sources.title: 'Enough Evidence': Centre Alleges Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka Receiving Foreign Funds; CJP Hits Back - News18
sources.articleText:
Union Minister Jitendra Singh has accused activists associated with the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) of receiving funds from unauthorised sources, including anti-India organisations within and outside the country, alleging that foreign-funded NGOs and “deep state operatives" are manufacturing a narrative against India.
Addressing the media in Bengaluru, Singh claimed that there was sufficient evidence to establish that individuals associated with the campaign were receiving money from overseas sources. He also named Abhijeet Dipke and Ashutosh Ranka while making allegations about their alleged financial links.
“There is enough evidence to show that they are being funded by unauthorised sources, by anti-India NGOs, and anti-India organisations within and outside the country. The foreign-funded NGOs, deep state operatives and anti-India forces are manufacturing this narrative," Singh said.
